Definition: adverb from G3956; entirely; specially, at all events, (with negative, following) in no event:--by all means, altogether, at all, needs, no doubt, in (no) wise, surely.
BiblicalUsage: Pantōs means altogether, entirely, by all means. Paul asks, Are we better than they? No, in no wise, for we have before proved both Jews and Gentiles that they are all under sin, and he says, I am made all things to all men, that I might by all means save some.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that altogether cuts both ways: all are altogether under sin, and Paul will use altogether every means to save some.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
